title: The Call of the Nations
english: Regarding the calling of the nations: for they were not called because of their own righteousness, but because of the philanthropy of the one calling.

He says, 'And thus, striving for honor, to preach the gospel not where Christ has been named, so that I might not build upon a foundation of another' (Rom 15), not as one avoiding the fellowship of the other apostles, but as one greedy and unjust, judging the works of others, to seize glory for himself.

He says, 'But I want you to be wise toward the good, and innocent toward the evil' (Rom 16:19); this is to use prudence so as not to be wronged by others, and innocence so as not to plot against others.

And the Lord also commanded this, saying: 'Become prudent as serpents and innocent as doves' (Matt 10:16). For indeed innocence and simplicity without prudence is foolishness, but prudence by itself [...]
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG Fragmenta in epistulam ad Romanos u04-rem-early

title: The Hidden Mystery and the Law
english: When integrity is approaching, one falls into wickedness.

In the ancient times, when error was trading in life and idolatry was prevailing, men did not even have the knowledge of the Pantokrator God; so much did they lack knowing our Lord Jesus Christ (Rom 16:25–27).

But Moses the lawgiver and the prophets, having been prepared to teach the truth—manifestly to the Jews, but according to the dispensation to the Gentiles—for this reason, according to the providence of God, many became captives and lived among the nations so that they might instruct them by their own conscience. The prophets, having been prepared to preach the Pantokrator God, the matter concerning the Only-begotten was still in a secret state, more mysterious by them [...]
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Proclamation of Christ's Knowledge
english: It is being handed down, and is almost known by them alone. Since at one time the nations were instructed through the mingling with the Jews to know the God over all, so also our Savior Jesus Christ, having come to dwell in the flesh among the world, sends his own disciples as his heralds of the knowledge.

While it was being obscured in the times, it is to be preached in the last times, who also, wandering everywhere, were announcing Christ God, begotten of God without beginning and without time, testifying at the same time by the holy and illuminating Spirit, that he completes the consubstantial Trinity, providing [it] from the Father through the Son unto men. Having been struck by the wisdom of his dispensation, he sends back the glory which is owed to God.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
